_comment: EVERY gameplay tunable in TROPHIC. Guardrail G11 / INV-4: no gameplay constant may be a literal in code — all read from this file. Retuning balance touches this file only (INV-3). Sources are cited per group; anything sourced 'build-doc addition' is explicitly tunable there.
_singleSource: No number in this file may also be written somewhere else in data/. Numbers the bible states FOR A NAMED MOVE (powers 40/70/50/60, Singe/Dous 20%, Regrow 30%, Trample +25, Terrify 2 turns) are CONTENT and live only in data/moves.json; magnitudes the bible names without numbering live only here, referenced from moves.json by `magnitudeKey`. tests/unit/transcription.test.ts gates both directions.

types._source: bible §1 — multiplier VALUES only; the chart SHAPE is content and lives in data/moves.json.

age._source: bible §2 age multiplier; bible §4 lifespan on catch; build-doc §3 L9 / §7.4 metamorphic jump.

stats._source: bible §2 — effective stat = Base × AgeMult × (1 + 0.02 × Level) + trait modifiers; traits are flat ±10%.

traits._source: bible §2 — 'Traits: flat ±10% modifiers with names ("Thick Pelt: +10% Defense"). 1 per wild creature, +1 slot via inheritance, Elders roll rare traits.' The MAGNITUDE is stats.traitModPct (never repeated per trait); the pool below carries only name/stat/direction/rarity. Rare traits are the Elder-only pool and are always beneficial — that is what makes an Elder roll worth having. Names other than 'Thick Pelt' (bible-verbatim) and 'Silk-Spun' (DEVIATIONS D7) are coined: DEVIATIONS D16, in scope for the G15 IP sweep.

damage._source: build-doc §7.4 damage roll; crit is driven by Instinct (bible §2) and is a build-doc-addition tunable.

status._source: build-doc §7.4 — Burn 6%/turn chip; Toxin 4% ramping +2%/turn; Soak −30% Speed; Daze 25% skip. One status at a time, newest wins. NOTE: the light-type-move apply chance is NOT here — bible §3 states it per move ('Singe (40, 20% Burn)'), so it is content and lives once, in data/moves.json.

moves._source: bible §3 — 'Each creature has exactly 4 move slots: 2 type moves + 1 role move + 1 utility, unlocked at levels 1/5/10/15'; build-doc §7.1 repeats the 1/5/10/15 in movePool slot order. Keyed by the movePool slot names so core/battle.ts can answer 'which moves does a level-7 creature know' from data alone (G11 / INV-4).

moveEffects._source: Magnitudes bible §3 names without numbering ('+Defense', '+evasion'). Moves reference these by magnitudeKey so no magnitude is a literal in code or duplicated in moves.json.

battle._source: MERGED AT INTEGRATION from data/balance.additions.A3.json (lane A3, core/battle.ts). bible §3 utility move Burrow/Roost — 'skip turn, +evasion'; build-doc §7.4 statuses + status.persistUntilCured.
battle._why: evadeTurns 1 = the evasion covers the turn the user spent skipping and no longer. (The evade also resolves BEFORE the opponent's attack — core/battle.ts `movePriority` — because an evade applied after the hit it is meant to duck mitigates nothing, which made the move strictly dominated for every creature slower than its opponent.) Any larger duration makes a 0-power utility move strictly better than attacking, which would break the §10.5 round-robin band. statusWearOffTurns is consulted ONLY when status.persistUntilCured is false: with the shipped `true` a status never wears off on its own (build-doc §7.4 names no expiry), so the number is inert at ship — it exists so that flipping the advertised flag in the balance harness actually changes behaviour instead of doing nothing.

catch._source: build-doc §7.4 catch formula (build-doc addition, tunable), AMENDED 2026-08-25 (DEVIATIONS D-A5-1, authorised by Hank): p = baseCatch(age) × snareTier × (baitMult × instinctBait) × (2 − hpFrac)/2 × lureMult, clamped.
catch._instinctBait: bible §2 gives Instinct three jobs — 'crit chance, bait success, sign-reading quality' — and until this amendment core/battle.ts read it for crit alone, which made Instinct the strongest and NEGATIVE predictor of round-robin win rate (r = -0.582, docs/BALANCE-REPORT.md §3.1). The bait term now scales with the CATCHING creature's Instinct: instinctBait = 1 + instinctBaitSlope × (insShare − instinctBaitPivot), where insShare = ins / (hp+atk+def+spd+ins) over that creature's EFFECTIVE stats. The SHARE, not the raw stat, is what a point of Instinct actually costs: every non-Ancient line spends exactly 300 base points (data/species.json _statRule), and because the age, level, metamorphic and Beast multipliers are common to all five stats they cancel out of the ratio — so the term reads ALLOCATION and cannot become a level-scaled global catch buff. In-battle stat mods are deliberately NOT read (raising your own Defense with Harden would otherwise lower your catch odds). instinctBaitPivot is the roster's MEDIAN Instinct allocation, 45/300 = 0.15, so a median-Instinct catcher is unchanged from the pre-amendment formula; measured over the 24 non-Ancient lines the term spans ×0.846 (base ins 30) to ×1.257 (base ins 70) with a roster mean of ×1.010. Positive over the whole mathematically possible share range [0,1] — 1 + 3×(0−0.15) = 0.55 — so the term never flips the sign of a probability; the .02–.95 clamp still binds at both ends.

medicine._source: bible §11 — 'Medicines — salve (field heal), tonic (status cure), inn rest (full heal, 2 ticks).' The bible names the effects without numbering them, so the magnitudes are build-doc-addition tunables. Item ids live here too so BattleAction {kind:"item", itemId} resolves without a literal in code (G11). Inn tick cost is clock.innTicks.

xp._source: build-doc §7.4 (build-doc addition, tunable): xpGain = 12 + 4×enemyLevel × ageBonus(E:1.3); xpToNext(l) = 15 × l^1.4; cap 40.

ecosim._source: build-doc §7.3 numbered population step. presence multipliers per bible §4 Ancients.
ecosim._demand: demand[s] = count[s] × demandPerIndividual[role of s] (role read at webRoleAgeClass). Per-ROLE because the pyramid is per-role: one global figure cannot make an Apex starve when its prey crash without starving every Mesopredator at the shipped state. A role whose value is 0 has NO live diet at all (bible §5: Producers photosynthesise, Scavengers 'eat nothing live', Ancients 'eat nothing') — for those the sim uses noDietFoodFactor and skips the §7.3 step-2 starvation check entirely, instead of dividing by zero or starving them to extinction. Values are calibrated against the shipped node counts so that (a) nothing starves at the shipped state and (b) any Apex whose derived prey pool falls to 10% crosses starveThreshold — build-doc §10.2 `cascade_emerges`. Both directions are gated by tests/unit/transcription.test.ts.
ecosim._starveTermination: MERGED AT INTEGRATION from data/balance.additions.A2.json. build-doc §7.3 steps 2 and 4 leave one gap between them: with `deaths = count × starveRate` alone, a starving population of 3 goes 2.1 → 1.47 → 1.03 → 0.72 and, under stochastic rounding, can sit at 1 individual indefinitely — so a crash never RESOLVES and `apex count → 0` (§10.2 `cascade_emerges`) is not a law, only a likelihood. These two keys make starvation terminal: a starving population loses at least one individual per season and does not breed while starving. Both are general rules over every species at every node (no species is named anywhere — G6); neither can fire at the shipped node states, where the lowest food ratio is 0.67 against a starveThreshold of 0.4.
ecosim._presenceEffects: MERGED AT INTEGRATION from data/balance.additions.A2.json. bible §4 states what each Ancient's presence does — Vellsire 'buffs all breeding rates in adjacent nodes (keystone)', Kilnback 'keeps the steppe vents warm (Fire spawns active)', Undermere 'steadies the marsh water table (Water breeding)'. The MAGNITUDES are keystoneBreedMult / ventWarmthBreedMult / waterTableBreedFloor above, but nothing said which type an effect acts on or whether it multiplies or floors — so both had to be decided in core/ecosim.ts, where `if (effect === "waterTable")` was a bare code literal (G11) that, because data/species.json carries exactly ONE line per effect name, was in practice `if (this is Undermere)` (G6). Both halves now live here: `mode` selects the SHAPE of the effect from a structural vocabulary (PRESENCE_MODES) that any number of Ancients could share, `type` names what it acts on, and `magnitudeKey` points at the number above rather than repeating it (DEVIATIONS D19 — one number, one home). Adding a fourth Ancient with an existing shape is a data edit (INV-1), not a code edit.

cascade._source: MERGED AT INTEGRATION from data/balance.additions.A2.json. build-doc §10.2 states the `cascade_emerges` property in numbers — 'forcing its primary prey to <10% for 2 consecutive seasons yields apex count →0 and mesopredator count strictly rising within 4 seasons'. They are thresholds of the CLAIM, not of the sim, so they live here rather than as literals in tests/property/ecosim.test.ts. `mesoReleaseSeasons` is the window the release clause is measured over, counted from the season the apex reaches 0.
cascade._coverage: The two coverage floors below are the property test's own thresholds, kept out of the test body for the same reason as the four above: they are claims about the shipped content, and a reviewer must be able to see what strength was claimed without reading a test. `mesoSurvivesForcingMinFraction` is the fraction of seeds in which a mesopredator whose forced target is at least one individual is still alive when the apex reaches 0 (measured at r4: 0.66). `releaseCoverageMinFraction` is the fraction of generated cascades in which anything survived to be released (measured: ~0.4).

clock._source: build-doc §3 L8, AMENDED 2026-08-25 (DEVIATIONS D-Q2-1, authorised by Hank) — 16-tick season meter; travel 1 / foray 1 / inn 2; year = FULL METER; 4 ticks per season. A gym victory no longer ends a year.
clock._yearsTotal: NOT A CAP. The calendar is unbounded — year may be 9 or 40 and nothing stops it (D-Q3-1). yearsTotal is the EXPECTED year count under normal pacing: six acts at roughly a year each, which is what the HUD quotes, what the balance harness drives by default, and what the six-year property trajectories measure. Story progression is the ACT model's (see `acts`), and no code may read this key to decide whether the run is over.

acts._source: THE SECOND CLOCK (DEVIATIONS D-Q3-1, authorised by Hank: 'the game should progress based on the player going through the gyms and side events, not based on year progression. Simply switch out the time check points for event check points.'). Acts are driven by badges and quest flags and NEVER by time; the calendar (see `clock`) is driven by ticks and never by acts. The rows below transcribe content-bible §6 (the six towns and their one route each, in order) and §7 (the six leaders, in order) — no town, route or leader is invented here (G2). The flag names are the ones data/dialogue.json already reads: `gym.<id>.beaten`, `story.opening.done`, `story.greaves.beaten`.
acts._act0: Act 0 is the prologue: a save that has not finished Maren's opening chain. It is a real, reachable state — a new save starts there — and it opens Hearthollow alone, which is bible §6's 'Warden Maren's field station: starter choice, bait-crafting intro, tutorial forage'. Act 1 opens when `story.opening.done` is set, at zero badges.
acts._noCap: `last` is the last act the region HAS, not a deadline. Nothing fails, expires or ends when the calendar passes it, and a player may sit in act 1 for twenty years.

regionalEvents._source: bible §9's four regional events, as SEASON-LONG WINDOWS. Hank, 2026-08-25: 'events like that last for a whole season and not just for one in-game day.' A window opens on a season boundary, stays open for clock.ticksPerSeason ticks and closes at the next boundary — core/regional-events.ts. The Annual Festival is the year's final season (bible §9 amended: it no longer CLOSES the year, it spans the season the meter fills in); the Great Migration is a migrant's seasonalWindow (data/species.json, already a season by construction); a Cullbrand raid's window is the season its ACT was entered in; a Bloom Year is a node whose flora clears the fraction below at a season boundary.
regionalEvents._bloomFraction: bible §9 'a route whose producers thrive gets bonus spawns' names no number. Expressed as a FRACTION of ecosim.floraMax rather than an absolute so it cannot become a second copy of that ceiling (this file's _singleSource rule). The BONUS-SPAWN half of §9's sentence is deliberately NOT implemented here: it is story-review decision D10 and unruled, so this ships the window and nothing weights an encounter by it (G2/G3).
regionalEvents._flagNames: A window publishes itself as the quest flag `<windowFlagPrefix><windowId><windowFlagSuffix>`. The names are chosen so the festival's flag is `event.festival.open` — the flag data/dialogue.json ALREADY reads and which, until now, nothing wrote (docs/STORY-REVIEW.md §5.1 lists it among the externally-granted flags). The other three publish the same shape: `event.migration.<lineId>.open`, `event.bloom.<nodeId>.open`, `event.raid.<raidId>.open`.

encounter._source: build-doc §7.2 derivations — weight = live population count, migrants filtered by season, Scavenger weight × (1 + recentDeaths/scavengerRecentDeathsDivisor). Rates are build-doc-addition tunables.
encounter._throughput: build-doc §4: 'A foray step rolls encounters' (plural) and §3 L8 charges a foray ONE tick — so a foray is an excursion of stepsPerForay encounter rolls, each at encounterChancePerStep, not a single roll. The pair is load-bearing: 16 ticks/year × stepsPerForay × encounterChancePerStep is the player's maximum encounters per year at one node, and the year-1 over-catch demo beat (build-doc §1, §15 I2) is only reachable if that budget beats the target populations' regrowth. Gated by tests/unit/transcription.test.ts.
encounter._levelByYear: RETUNED 2026-08-25 from [4,10,16,22,28,34] (DEVIATIONS D-A5-G3, INV-3: balance.json only). The gym ramp in data/gyms.json is 8/14/20/26/32/38, so the old array put the region's own wild population FOUR levels under the leader it feeds — measured, that is why the harness's UNTRAINED player (docs/BALANCE-REPORT.md §1 clause 4) won gym 1 in 0.2% of 500 seeds. The new array is the same smooth +6 ramp two levels under the gym instead of four: a player who only catches and walks in is behind, not hopeless. Measured over 500 seeds/gym: UNTRAINED Maribel 1.6% → 31.4%, mean UNTRAINED gym win rate +11.7 pp, and every TRAINED row byte-identical (the TRAINED model reads gyms.json, not this key), so no gym is moved out of a §10.5 band.
encounter._levelByYearIsAnActLadder: THE KEY NAME IS HISTORY; BOTH READERS INDEX IT BY ACT (DEVIATIONS D-Q3-2 as resolved, D-Q3-8). tools/harness/player.ts has always read it by the LEADER'S act, and D-A5-G3 tuned these six values against the gym ramp, which is an act ladder. game/encounters.ts `rollLevel` read it by the CALENDAR YEAR until 2026-08-25, which under an unbounded decoupled calendar meant a player still in act 1 on Route 1 in calendar year 6 met level 34-38 wild creatures against heirs entering at ~5 — a soft fail state by the back door, and the exact pressure Q3 removed. It reads the ACT now, so the two readings agree and the array means one thing. The KEY is not renamed because that is data + core/types.ts + core/schemas.ts + tools/harness, all outside the change that found it; this note is the name.

retirement._source: build-doc §7.5 step 3 — HEIR (level = floor(parent×0.5), inherits 1–2 traits) or BOON (+10% to one stat).
retirement._boonMagnitude: The BOON's +10% is stats.boonModPct and lives ONLY there. A `retirement.boonStatPct` duplicate existed until integration and was deleted per this file's own _singleSource rule and DEVIATIONS D-A4-13: core/battle.ts read stats.boonModPct while core/lifecycle.ts read retirement.boonStatPct, so retuning either alone made the creature card and the battle disagree.
retirement._heirLevelMin: MERGED AT INTEGRATION from data/balance.additions.A4.json. build-doc §7.5 step 3: HEIR level = floor(parentLevel × heirLevelFactor), which gives 0 for a level-1 parent. bible §2 states 'Levels 1–40', so the minimum is 1. encounter.minLevel is NOT reusable here — that is the floor on WILD encounter levels (2), a different rule.
retirement._boonMaxStacks: MERGED AT INTEGRATION from data/balance.additions.A4.json. build-doc §7.5 step 3 gives the BOON a size (+10% to one stat) but no count, so nothing bounded it: a full party of six Elders retiring on the same turn — which is exactly what happens to a party caught together in year 1 — could put six boons on one survivor for +60% to a single stat, and the save validated. The unit of the rule is the bible §2 trait modifier (±10%) and the trait system's own ceiling is traits.maxSlots = 2, so 2 is the matching ceiling here: any one stat can be lifted by at most +20% from legacies.

yearEvents._source: MERGED AT INTEGRATION from data/balance.additions.A4.json. build-doc §7.5 step 5: 'node sims run their 4th season step + year events (Cullbrand raid scripts decrement scripted node populations)'. bible §9 'Cullbrand Harvest raids (scripted per act, populations visibly drop at a named node)'. The raids are DATA, never code: the game only applies whatever this list says. G6 note — a raid may only decrement the harvested populations; it must never touch the predators above them. The predator collapse that makes Cindershelf's arrival read as 'mid-collapse' has to EMERGE from the build-doc §7.3 rules once the prey are gone, which is exactly why the numbers below stop at the two Grazer lines.
yearEvents._actKeyed: RE-KEYED FROM `year` TO `act` 2026-08-25 (DEVIATIONS D-Q3-1). bible §9 always said 'scripted per ACT'; the field said year because content-bible §6 equated the two. A raid now fires on ENTRY to its act, so Cindershelf is entered mid-collapse whether the player arrives in calendar year 2 or year 11. The group keeps the name `yearEvents` because build-doc §7.5 step 5 names it that.
yearEvents._standingStock: A STRIP-HARVEST TAKES THE STANDING STOCK, NOT A FIXED BODY COUNT (DEVIATIONS D-Q6-1). Re-keying the raid to the act (`_actKeyed`) made it fire whenever the player earns the act — but the per-target `remove` figures below were authored against r4's SHIPPED counts, and a locked node still breeds every season while the player is elsewhere. Measured through core/ecosim.ts on the shipped r4: arriving at act 4 in calendar year 1 the raid leaves the Grazer tier at 5 of 24 and the Apex reaches 0 in 39 of 64 seeds; arriving in year 4 (the harness's one-act-per-year pacing) the same script leaves 14 of 33 standing and the Apex reaches 0 in 1 of 64; by year 7 the node is at carrying capacity and the Apex never goes at all. So the act-keyed raid did NOT make bible §6's 'arrival mid-collapse' true at every arrival — it made it true at exactly one. `harvestFractionOfStanding` is what fixes that: the harvest is `max(target.remove, round(count × fraction))`, so the authored body count is the floor of the harvest and the fraction carries it at any standing stock. THE NUMBER IS READ OUT OF THE AUTHORED SCRIPT, NOT CHOSEN (G2 / DEVIATIONS D9): the shipped raid removes 11 of 14 Ashvole (0.786) and 8 of 10 Cragmar (0.800), and 0.8 reproduces BOTH authored removes exactly at the shipped state — round(0.8×14)=11, round(0.8×10)=8 — so nothing about the beat as authored moves. G6 is untouched: the fraction scales only what the script harvests, and the collapse above it still has to emerge from the §7.3 rules.

raids._source: bible §6 act 4, Cindershelf: 'arrival mid-collapse — Route 4's web already crashed by Cullbrand strip-harvest'. This is the only raid the bible pins to a named node and act; the remaining per-act raids are content another lane must author into this list, not numbers to invent here.

overlayDiff._source: build-doc §8.2 / §9.5 — IoU ≥ 0.85 on dilated Sobel edges within walkable cells; denoise 0.35 stepping −0.05 to a 0.2 floor; ≤3 regen attempts.

map._source: build-doc §7.6 — virtual 480×320 integer-scaled; painted maps 1024² rendered 2×; mask sampled on a 16px grid (64×64 cells); player 32×48, tile step 32.

party._source: build-doc §3 L12 / §7.8 — versioned JSON in localStorage, 3 slots.
party._saveVersion: BUMPED 1 → 2 on 2026-08-25 with the two-clock change (DEVIATIONS D-Q3-7). core/acts.ts `story.actEntered` is the latch that says which acts a save has already ENTERED, and a save written before it exists has no latch — so `lastActEntered` reads `first - 1` and the game re-enters acts 0..N on the first frame, re-applying the act-4 Cullbrand raid ON TOP of the harvest the old build already applied. Measured on a mid-run v1 save (3 badges, r4 already harvested once): ashvole 3 → 0, cragmar 2 → 0, recentDeaths 19 → 24, i.e. an extinction the player did not cause, which then feeds the derived cascade. A new save is indistinguishable from an old one by questFlags alone (both have no latch), so the VERSION is the only thing that can tell them apart. core/save.ts `deserialize` refuses a v1 save with the documented message; saves are not migrated (demo scope).

economy._source: bible §11 — snares ×3 tiers, baits role-generic vs species-specific, medicines, inn rest. Prices are build-doc-addition tunables; medicine EFFECTS are in `medicine`.

audio._source: bible §12a procedural treatments — season DSP presets and progressive year darkening.

harness._source: build-doc §10.5 — gym win-rate targets 80–95 / 60–80 / 45–65 by pair, round-robin flags outside 35–65%, 500 seeds.

overcatch._source: build-doc §1 demo beat 1 (never-cut) + §15 I2: 'cascade demo reproducible from overcatch-script.json in real play'. This group states the reference player the feasibility gate assumes — a determined player working ONE walkable node, using the snare tier and bait below and throwing at referenceHpFrac. The gate (tests/unit/transcription.test.ts) requires that this player can drive an Apex's derived prey pool under the starvation threshold within yearsBudget years DESPITE regrowth.

perf._source: build-doc §12 — ecosim.step all 12 nodes < 5ms with ×4 margin on mega-node; battle reducer < 1ms/action; save serialize < 50ms; boot < 3s.

rng._source: build-doc §8.1 — one seeded xorshift128 stream per subsystem, seeds derived from save seed + subsystem tag. the seeded stream is the only source of randomness in the project (G11).
